composition: Nominal composition Fe–20Mn–6Al–0.6C–0.15Si (wt.%, as given in the paper; the same composition is used for the austenitic low-density designation). Fe is the balance/base element. Al (6 wt%) is the light-weighting addition — per the paper's introduction, each 1.0 wt% Al reduces density by about 1.3% — and, being present at a relatively high level, it also raises the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the austenite to a relatively high value. Mn (20 wt%) and C (0.6 wt%) are the alloying elements that, together with Al, give the fully austenitic (single-phase fcc) constituent observed in the as-forged state; Si is present at 0.15 wt%. The composition is that used in the density estimation (composition terms in wt.%) and in the thermodynamic SFE calculation (in mole fractions).
summary: The as-forged (initial) state of a Fe–20Mn–6Al–0.6C–0.15Si austenitic low-density steel. It was produced by vacuum induction melting and casting, homogenized at 1250 °C for 2 h, forged into 60 mm-diameter round bars between 1100 and 950 °C, and furnace cooled to room temperature. It is the fully austenitic base material (precursor) from which the cryogenic tensile and Charpy impact specimens of this study were taken, and it establishes the reference microstructure and stacking fault energy against which the temperature-dependent deformation behavior and mechanical properties were interpreted.
